trace.final_message:
The contact sheet function is in and committed as `7774cf0`. All 31 tests pass, with 1 skipped that was already skipped before.

`contact_rows(students)` in `rosterkit/contacts.py` returns a list of text rows, each with display name, section and email, sorted by display name. Columns are padded to the widest entry in each column, so they line up.

A student with a missing or blank email raises `ContactError` with a message like `no email for Doe, Jo`. An empty list also raises `ContactError`. `ContactError` is a subclass of the existing `ProjectError`.

`tests/test_contacts.py` has five tests covering sorting, column alignment, a missing email naming the student, a blank email, and an empty list. One of my own tests failed on the first run because it assumed the wrong sort order. I fixed the test, not the code.

The new files follow the project rules in `CLAUDE.md`. That means reverse-sorted imports, functions of 8 lines or fewer, lines of 60 characters or fewer, and no trailing commas or double blank lines. As a result, the top-level functions are separated by a single blank line, not the usual two.

I tried to add a line to `CHANGES.txt` under Unreleased, but the `sed` command failed on macOS. That file is unchanged, so the commit holds only the two new files. Say so if you want the changelog entry added.
